title: Nasdaq-100 Index Futures: Intraday Momentum or Reversal?
provenance: Academic; Journal of Investment Management / author SSRN record
access: Author abstract
assessment: Prior-session and overnight returns interact with return signs and calendar conditions. Exact full regression specification was not accessible; R3 uses an explicitly new causal reconstruction. R1/R2 used sign filters instead.

title: Assessing the Profitability of Timely Opening Range Breakout on Index Futures Markets
access: Primary conference predecessor full-text search and published DOI metadata
assessment: Already underlies R1 ORB04. A different entry sequence can be studied, but this does not repair unresolved first-touch ordering or validate a retest strategy.

title: Assessing the profitability of intraday opening range breakout strategies
access: Publisher abstract and methodology excerpts
assessment: Statistical thresholds and contraction/expansion rationale. Original findings are time-dependent; not direct NQ evidence. R1 ORB06 already reconstructs this family.

title: Day Trading Returns Across Volatility States
provenance: Umea University working paper; later IFTA publication
access: Author-institution PDF abstract
assessment: Volatility conditions matter for ORB. Does not establish that any particular observable opening-range filter predicts profit. R1/R2 already test volatility gating.

title: Evolutionary ORB-based model with protective closing strategies
access: Bibliographic record; full publisher text unavailable
assessment: Existing R1 ORB07 source. Genetic search is an optimization technique, not an additional economic edge. No new model slot.

title: Neural Network-Based ORB Strategies for Threshold Classification on Taiwan Futures Market
access: IEEE presentation record and conference contents
assessment: Existing R1 ORB08 source. Metadata reviewed; full method not newly verified. Neural thresholds do not count as a newly discovered mechanism.

title: Enhancing Opening Range Breakout Strategies with LSTM-Based True Range Prediction
access: Author conference abstract; not full paper
assessment: Predictive volatility improves a threshold strategy in the authors' study. Future-TR oracle results are not executable. R1 ORB09 uses a gradient-boosting surrogate, not the source LSTM.

title: Market Intraday Momentum
access: Author SSRN abstract and institutional publication record
assessment: First-half-hour return measured from the prior close predicts the final half-hour in the source sample. NQ transfer must be tested; opening-only return is a separate ablation.

title: Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum
provenance: Journal of Financial Economics; Robeco / Erasmus / Notre Dame
access: Full author-hosted PDF downloaded; relevant methods inspected
assessment: Direct futures evidence for late-day momentum. R2 CLOSE_MOMENTUM already uses prior-close-to-entry return, so repeating that signal gets no new discovery slot. Dealer-position data are not available.

title: Understanding Intraday Momentum Strategies
market: Includes S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and DJIA futures
access: Publisher abstract, data statement and author publication record; full model unavailable
assessment: Unconditional overnight-to-close predictability disappears out of sample in the paper. Regime and signal-strength conditioning motivate a competing model, not a blanket positive result. Our filtered-state implementation is an adaptation.

title: Profitability of Technical Stock Trading: Has It Moved from Daily to Intraday Data?
access: Full institutional working paper downloaded; methods inspected
assessment: Historical moving-average, momentum and RSI systems; performance weakens in later periods. Intraday sampling does not imply positions always close daily. No generic indicator ensemble is admitted on this evidence alone.

title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy for the U.S. Equity Market
access: Prior project primary-source review and source register
assessment: Stocks-in-play selection is central. A single NQ contract cannot replicate the stock-selection opportunity set. R2 opening direction and relative-volume models are adaptations.

title: Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)
provenance: Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper 24-97; Concretum / St. Gallen / Peak Capital
access: Author abstract plus prior project primary-method review
assessment: Time-of-day noise bands and dynamic exits deserve a fuller implementation. R2 fixed ATR stops and one-entry restriction changed the strategy materially; its missing-path flags also prevent a clean conclusion.

title: Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP): The Holy Grail for Day Trading Systems
provenance: Practitioner working paper; Concretum / Peak Capital
access: Author abstract and prior project primary-source review
assessment: Standalone VWAP direction strategy, not an ORB filter. Headline leveraged-ETF returns are not NQ forecasts. Bar-derived VWAP is only an approximation to transaction VWAP.

title: Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable?
access: Author abstract and author research summary
assessment: Modified opening-range strategy. Already represented in prior ORB work. ETF leverage, execution, and returns cannot be copied to prop-firm NQ accounts.

title: Intraday Price Reversals in the US Stock Index Futures Market: A 15-Year Study
access: Publisher abstract and methodology excerpts
assessment: Opening-gap reversals follow initial continuation, but transaction costs sharply weaken significance. R2 already tests fixed gap and opening-shock fades. Supports a comparator for statistical gap classification.

title: Statistical Arbitrage with Mean-Reverting Overnight Price Gaps on High-Frequency Data of the S&P 500
provenance: Journal of Risk and Financial Management; Erlangen-Nurnberg
market: S&P 500 index event study; constituent-stock trading
access: Full paper downloaded; event detection and trading sections inspected
assessment: Uses jump tests rather than a fixed gap cutoff. Prior-day intraday returns plus the current opening gap can define a causal event. NQ lacks constituent selection; R3 is a single-instrument transfer, not the paper's statistical-arbitrage portfolio.

title: Evidence and Behaviour of Support and Resistance Levels in Financial Time Series
provenance: Academic preprint; Imperial / Nottingham affiliations in manuscript
market: EURUSD, LLOY equity and Brent price series
access: Full author preprint downloaded; algorithms and sample inspected
assessment: Prior bounce count and age relate to subsequent bounces. Source is not NQ and does not establish executable net trading profits. Causal level discovery and next-bar execution are required.

title: Support for Resistance: Technical Analysis and Intraday Exchange Rates
provenance: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Economic Policy Review
access: Primary institutional source located
assessment: Level-related trend interruptions provide contextual support. FX evidence does not validate NQ levels, opening-range retests, or net profits.

title: Currency Orders and Exchange-Rate Dynamics: An Explanation for the Predictive Success of Technical Analysis
provenance: NY Fed Staff Report 125 / Journal of Finance
access: Primary institutional research record
assessment: Stop and take-profit order clustering offers a possible mechanism for continuation or reversal at levels. Our OHLCV data do not reveal those orders; avoid claims of measured stop hunts.

title: Intraday Patterns in the Cross-section of Stock Returns
provenance: Journal of Finance; academic authors, PanAgora research funding acknowledged
access: Author manuscript abstract, funding statement and publication record
assessment: Same-clock half-hour return continuation motivates a time-series NQ transfer. The paper's cross-sectional finding does not establish an aggregate-index effect. Net executable edge may be absent.

title: The Overnight Drift
provenance: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report 917
access: Primary abstract; prior project full-method review
assessment: European-opening drift and inventory interpretation already motivated R2. A DST correction or extra time filter is not a new discovery family; retain as later implementation work.

title: The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
provenance: Journal of Finance / Federal Reserve Bank of New York
access: Primary institutional abstract
assessment: Calendar-event mechanism is credible, but a cash-session-only NQ transfer has a much smaller exposure window and very few events in our short history. Requires a separately frozen event calendar and more data.

title: Time Series Momentum
access: Primary institutional research summary
assessment: Long-horizon futures evidence. A 12-month/next-month result is not evidence for a five-minute NQ rule; no intraday model slot on that basis.

title: Enhancing Time Series Momentum Strategies Using Deep Neural Networks
access: Author preprint abstract
assessment: Deep Momentum Networks concern a much larger futures panel and a different horizon. Our short single-instrument sample cannot justify a faithful transfer.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Trading
access: Author preprint abstract
assessment: Interesting methodology, but reward optimization does not itself supply an edge. Dataset scale, costs and daily-flattening differences make it unsuitable for a new NQ-only slot now.

title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study
access: Full author preprint downloaded; abstract and methods inspected
assessment: Fourteen tested families fail the author's joint criteria. Useful warning, not a proof that all OHLCV strategies are impossible. Positive-control claims are not adopted without reproducible specifications. Already cited in R1 ORB03.

title: A Validated Volatility-Volume-Gap Classifier for Regime Identification in MNQ Intraday Data
access: Full author preprint downloaded and inspected
assessment: The paper reports failed trading variants. Unreconciled counts include 40 classifier days, yearly counts totaling 55, and 125 days in another analysis. First-30-minute return is observable at 10:00, not premarket. Do not use the title as evidence of a validated tradable edge.

title: Sequential Structure in Intraday Futures Data: LSTM vs Gradient Boosting on MNQ
access: Full author preprint downloaded; abstract inspected
assessment: No tested architecture has significant out-of-sample accuracy above the stated base rate. This does not rule out all ML, but it argues against selecting an LSTM simply for sophistication.

title: Market Simulation under Adverse Selection
access: Author preprint record
assessment: Fill probability and adverse selection matter. Market making needs order-level inputs and queue/fill modeling that our one-minute OHLCV data cannot supply.

title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
authors: Bailey; Borwein; Lopez de Prado; Zhu
provenance: Journal of Computational Finance; academic/institutional methodology
access: Author-hosted paper/source record
assessment: Retain the full trial universe and account for selection. PBO is a diagnostic, not a substitute for causal execution or a genuinely untouched test.

title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
access: Author SSRN abstract
assessment: Adjust for search and non-normal returns; dependence assumptions and effective trial count must be disclosed. Do not treat every correlated grid row as an independent strategy.

title: Anatomy of the Retest in the QQQ Opening Range Breakout
access: Author SSRN abstract; full specification not accessed
assessment: Directly studies breakout/retest sequences, but explicitly makes no exploitability or causality claim. NQ entries, risk rules and timing below are our proposed hypothesis, not a replicated institutional system.

title: Information Shares for Markets with Partially Overlapping Trading Hours
market: S&P 500 / Nasdaq cash and E-mini markets
access: Publisher method and conclusion excerpts
assessment: Relevant to price discovery, but requires synchronized cash/futures inputs. It does not show that ES reliably leads NQ at our execution horizon.

title: Improving Performance with Fast Alphas: A Tactical Overlay for Intraday Trend Trading
access: Primary author summary and indexed paper excerpts
assessment: The standalone short-horizon reversal signal loses money after transaction costs in the authors study; they instead investigate delaying trend entries and exits. Retain as a possible later execution overlay after a base NQ signal survives, not an independent tenth edge.

title: Goldman Sachs New Horizons Index: Satellite Intraday Equity Component
provenance: Official bank methodology; not an academic paper
market: Explicit standalone NQ and ES components
access: Full 105-page public PDF downloaded; pages 87-88 inspected
assessment: NQ component GSISMRNQ reacts to moves from the previous close, uses delayed TWAP rebalancing and ends flat. This overview omits numerical subcomponent parameters; our transparent version must not be called an exact replica or endorsed strategy.

title: Morgan Stanley Non-Financial US Large Cap Short-Only Intraday Momentum Series 3 Index
provenance: Official bank description in SEC filing; not an academic paper
access: Primary filing, pages 20-21 inspected
assessment: Short-only, previous-close threshold exposure, scaled with price movement and volatility, flat overnight. Corroborates institutional use of the mechanism. Treated within I01's family rather than an extra independent edge; 0.0001 in the table is a transaction-cost rate, not the signal threshold.
